note: Primary sources checked for the flagship lesson. 'checked' is the date the page was fetched and read for the claims listed. A URL alone does not make a claim verified.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.supports: Workflows follow predefined code paths; agents let the model direct its own process and tool use in a loop on environmental feedback; agents can pause for human feedback; stopping conditions such as iteration limits keep control.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.supports: Context is the set of tokens sent when sampling the model and is a finite resource; just-in-time retrieval; structured notes kept outside the context window; sub-agents return condensed summaries.

sources.title: Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills
sources.supports: Skills are folders of instructions, scripts and resources loaded progressively when relevant; install from trusted sources and audit them.

sources.title: Handling stop reasons
sources.supports: stop_reason values (end_turn, max_tokens, stop_sequence, tool_use, pause_turn, refusal, model_context_window_exceeded) describe why a response ended.

sources.title: Hooks reference
sources.supports: Hooks are handlers on lifecycle events; some events can block (PreToolUse permissionDecision allow/deny/ask), others only observe; hook types include command, http, mcp_tool, prompt (model-evaluated) and agent.

sources.title: Subagents
sources.supports: Each subagent runs in its own context window; subagents inherit the main conversation's tools unless restricted with tools / disallowedTools; worktree isolation is a filesystem copy, not an OS sandbox.

sources.title: MCP architecture overview
sources.supports: Host, client and server roles (one client per server connection); data layer (JSON-RPC) and transport layer; server primitives tools, resources, prompts; MCP covers context exchange, not how the application uses the model. Page served as protocol version 2026-07-28.

sources.title: MCP specification: Authorization
sources.supports: Authorization is optional; defined for HTTP transports with OAuth 2.1; the MCP server is a resource server that must validate token audience; insufficient scope returns 403; step-up retries should be limited.

sources.title: MCP security best practices
sources.supports: Token passthrough is forbidden; confused deputy risks; scope minimization and progressive least privilege; servers must not treat possession of a state handle as authentication.

sources.title: Prompting best practices
sources.supports: Setting a role in the system prompt focuses behaviour and tone; clear, explicit instructions and the reason behind them improve results; relevant, diverse examples are one of the most reliable ways to steer format and structure.

sources.title: Glossary
sources.supports: Tokens are the smallest units a model processes (words, subwords, characters or bytes); for Claude a token is about 3.5 English characters, varying by language. The context window is distinct from training data. Pretraining predicts the next word on a large unlabeled corpus, and pretrained models are not inherently good at following instructions; fine-tuning further trains a pretrained model on additional data; RLHF trains a model toward human preferences from rankings of example outputs; the Claude API does not currently offer fine-tuning.

sources.title: Reduce hallucinations
sources.supports: Allow the model to say it does not know, ground answers in direct quotes, verify claims with citations, restrict answers to provided documents; these reduce hallucinations but do not eliminate them, so validate critical information.

sources.title: Mitigate jailbreaks and prompt injections
sources.supports: For indirect injection: keep untrusted content in tool results, say what it is and where it came from, state the policy in the system prompt, screen tool outputs before acting, red-team the agent, and combine strategies. The steps strengthen guardrails; none is presented as complete.

sources.title: Updates to the OECD's definition of an AI system explained
sources.supports: An AI system is a machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers from the input it receives how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions; systems vary in autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment (definition updated November 2023).

sources.title: Deep learning
sources.supports: Deep learning uses models composed of multiple processing layers that learn representations at multiple levels of abstraction; backpropagation indicates how a machine should change its internal parameters; supervised learning is the most common form of machine learning.

sources.title: Attention Is All You Need
sources.supports: The Transformer is based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions; input tokens are converted to vectors with learned embeddings; layers are stacked.

sources.title: Embeddings
sources.supports: Text embeddings are numerical representations of text that enable measuring semantic similarity, used for search, recommendations and anomaly detection. Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model.

sources.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
sources.supports: Preference modelling and reinforcement learning from human feedback train language models to act as helpful and harmless assistants; preference models and policies can be updated iteratively with fresh feedback.

sources.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
sources.supports: A set of written principles guides training: a supervised phase of self-critique and revision, then reinforcement learning from AI feedback, where a model compares pairs of responses to create preference data.

sources.title: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence (SP 1270)
sources.supports: AI bias has systemic, statistical or computational, and human sources; data used to train and test systems may not be representative of the populations they affect.
